Duration is included in stage_complete console output
progress_snapshot shows completed/total WP counts and elapsed time
Existing event type formatting is unchanged
No crashes on missing or unexpected fields in log entries

summary: Added _format_duration(seconds: float | None) -> str helper function to orchestrator/src/utils/logging.py — handles None, 0, sub-minute, multi-minute, and multi-hour values with whole-second rounding.

Added _build_stream_console_line(entry) module-level helper to logging.py — produces rich console output for all 7 new event types: stage_start, stage_complete (enriched with duration_s), wp_status_change, wp_complete, progress_snapshot, pipeline_result, rework_detected.

Updated stream_entry to delegate console formatting to _build_stream_console_line — eliminates duplicated inline parts-building logic; all non-listed event types fall through to identical legacy format (no regressions).

Created orchestrator/tests/test_logging.py with 48 tests covering _format_duration edge cases, all 7 new event format patterns, existing event type stability, and robustness against missing/null fields.
All 370 orchestrator tests pass (370 passed, 1 pre-existing skip).

comments.note: orchestrator/src/utils/logging.py: _build_stream_console_line is a module-level function (not a class method), making it directly importable in tests without needing a WorkflowLogger instance. This is intentional and follows the same pattern as _slugify and _format_duration.

orchestrator/src/utils/logging.py: The log() method still contains its own inline parts-building logic (separate from stream_entry). Both methods share the same default format, so extracting log() to also call _build_stream_console_line would be a clean follow-up, but it is out of scope for this WP since log() is not a streaming path and was not listed in the spec.

summary: Ran 48 tests in tests/test_logging.py — all pass (0.12s); all 7 new event types verified against spec patterns.
Ran full orchestrator suite (374 passed, 1 pre-existing skip, 0 failures) — no regressions.

All 6 acceptance criteria confirmed: _format_duration handles None/0/sub-minute/multi-minute/multi-hour; all 7 event types produce correct structured output; duration present in stage_complete; progress_snapshot shows completed/total and elapsed; existing event formatting unchanged; no crashes on missing/null fields.

Edge-case stress tests passed: empty files list in pipeline_result correctly omitted, max_iterations=0 suppresses iter segment, no empty parentheses on minimal stage_complete, float boundaries round correctly.

comments.note: orchestrator/src/utils/logging.py: _format_duration uses Python's banker's rounding (round()), so _format_duration(0.5) returns '0s' (rounds to even 0) rather than '1s'. The spec says 'always round to whole seconds' without specifying tie-breaking. Not a defect — just an observable behavior for sub-second precision inputs, which are unlikely in practice.

No observations beyond the above. Code is clean, well-structured, and consistent with the module conventions established in WP-002/WP-003. The _build_stream_console_line helper follows the same module-level pattern as _slugify and _format_duration, making it directly testable without a WorkflowLogger instance.

summary: Reviewed orchestrator/src/utils/logging.py and orchestrator/tests/test_logging.py for WP-007 (console output formatting for new event types).
All 6 acceptance criteria confirmed met. No blocking issues found.
_format_duration is clean and handles all spec boundary cases correctly (None, 0, sub-minute, multi-minute, multi-hour) using idiomatic divmod.

_build_stream_console_line is well-structured as a module-level function consistent with the existing _slugify/_format_duration pattern, making it directly unit-testable. The None-guard pattern (or "") and the 'is not None' guard for numeric fields (tokens_used, rework_count) are both correct and handle zero-valued fields properly.
stream_entry delegation to _build_stream_console_line is clean; fallback path preserves all existing event behavior with no regressions.

48-test suite is comprehensive: every event type has full-format, minimal-fields, and no-crash tests. Strictness distribution is appropriate (exact equality for _format_duration, in-assertions for format tests).

comments.note: orchestrator/src/utils/logging.py: log() and stream_entry() now have duplicated default console formatting logic — log() builds parts inline while stream_entry() delegates to _build_stream_console_line(). The implementation correctly flags this as out-of-scope since log() is not a streaming path, but unifying both through _build_stream_console_line in a future cleanup pass would eliminate the duplication and ensure format consistency across both write paths.

orchestrator/src/utils/logging.py (_build_stream_console_line, rework_detected branch): agent_role is normalized via .lower().replace(' ', '_'), producing 'security_auditor' for multi-word roles like 'Security Auditor'. The spec examples only show single-word roles ('developer'). The normalization is reasonable, but documenting the expected slug format (or aligning with the PIPELINE_AGENT_MAP convention from the MCP server) would future-proof this if new multi-word roles are added.
